symptom: `$m = minimum $Items by DueDate;` over a DateTime attribute passed check and exec; mx check failed it with CE0016 "Attribute must be of type Autonumber, Decimal, Integer, or Long." at the Aggregate list activity.
cause: check and the builder judged an aggregate's attribute only for existence (#1646, flowMemberVerdict), never for type.
fix: Both refuse sum/average/minimum/maximum BY an attribute whose type is not AutoNumber, Decimal, Integer or Long, with one shared message. check reads the type from the script's declaration or the project; the builder from the declaring entity it already resolves. An unreadable type is not judged. `mxcli syntax microflow list-operations` names the allowed types.
insight: Measured on 11.12.6 with one script of nine microflows — the four functions over a DateTime and over a String attribute (8 x CE0016) plus an Integer control (clean) — and the new check refuses exactly the eight. assertAgree needs exec to refuse too: check -p alone is not exec's gate here, the builder is, so a rule added only to the checker passes check tests and still writes.
test: mdl/executor/aggregate_attribute_type_2528_test.go (refusals through check and exec; numeric and inherited controls)
